title: AI workflows for TypeScript — Oribos
description: AI workflows in TypeScript: typed steps, validated boundaries, and JSON snapshots that resume a run in another process.
h1: AI workflows — typed steps, validated boundaries, and runs that survive a restart.

sections.heading: Steps that promise what they take and what they give back
sections.body: A step declares its input and output schemas; the builder composes steps with then, parallel, branch and foreach. Every boundary — start input, step input, resume data — is validated before your code runs.

sections.heading: Agents join as steps, not instead of them
sections.body: A step can call an agent, run deterministic code, or both: use a model where you need reasoning, and a plain function where you don't. The workflow is what turns a multi-step process into something repeatable.

sections.heading: Suspend, resume, and move the run to another process
sections.body: ctx.suspend() unwinds a run with a JSON snapshot at a step boundary; resuming later — even from another process — continues from that snapshot. Snapshots go through a storage port that defaults to memory and takes adapters when persistence matters.

sections.heading: Runs you can watch while they happen
sections.body: start() yields lifecycle events at run and step boundaries, and the run settles to success, failed or suspended — progress is legible without inspecting internal state.

faq.question: When should I use a workflow instead of an agent?
faq.answer: Use a workflow when the process is defined up front and order, data flow, or validation matters; use an agent when the task is open-ended and the model should choose the next step. They compose: a workflow step can call an agent.

faq.question: Do workflows need a database or a queue?
faq.answer: No. The snapshot store defaults to an in-memory implementation and is swapped for an adapter — such as @oribos/sqlite — only when you want snapshots to outlive the process.

faq.question: What happens if my process restarts mid-run?
faq.answer: Runs suspend at step boundaries with a JSON snapshot, so with a persistent store you can resume the run from another process.

faq.question: Can steps run in parallel?
faq.answer: Yes: parallel runs steps together and foreach maps over a collection with controlled concurrency, while branch routes between paths.

faq.question: How do I pass data between steps?
faq.answer: Each step's output is the next step's typed input, and every boundary is validated against its schema before your code runs — a malformed value fails at the boundary, not deep inside a step.
